question: An internal communications lead has a month of scattered Claude answers about an office relocation and must turn them into one reference page for staff. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) Gather the relevant answers and drop the ones that no longer apply; decide what staff need to be able to look up about the move; have Claude organise the surviving material into a single artifact; check that artifact against the questions staff are actually asking.

B) Have Claude organise the surviving material into a single artifact; decide what staff need to be able to look up about the move; gather the relevant answers and drop the ones that no longer apply; check that artifact against the questions staff are actually asking.

C) Decide what staff need to be able to look up about the move; have Claude organise the surviving material into a single artifact; gather the relevant answers and drop the ones that no longer apply; check that artifact against the questions staff are actually asking.

D) Decide what staff need to be able to look up about the move; gather the relevant answers and drop the ones that no longer apply; have Claude organise the surviving material into a single artifact; check that artifact against the questions staff are actually asking.
correct_answers: D) Decide what staff need to be able to look up about the move; gather the relevant answers and drop the ones that no longer apply; have Claude organise the surviving material into a single artifact; check that artifact against the questions staff are actually asking.
explanations: Curation begins before she knows what the page is for, so relevance is judged against nothing and the decision about what staff need arrives after the material has already been filtered.
The artifact is assembled first, so a month of unfiltered and partly outdated answers is what gets organised, and the culling happens after the page has been built from them.
The scope is set correctly but the artifact is built before the outdated answers have been removed, so superseded relocation details are carried straight into the reference page staff will rely on.

Correct. What staff need to look up defines relevance, which is what makes the culling of stale answers meaningful; only then is there a clean set to organise into an artifact; and checking the finished page against real questions confirms it does the job it was scoped to do.
